correctness.rationale: The exact comparison holds on the full finite parameter domain. After j decisions in an urn of size M, the discrepancy of selection probabilities is |jk/M-a|/(M-j) ≤ j/(M-j). Couple the whole marked-location vectors while they agree, then sum over urns and times. The stationary law is obtained by uniform placement of red labels, even for periodic swaps; applying the same sampling argument once with M=N and subset size m gives the stationary term. Projection to counts and the reverse triangle inequality give (1). The two-state recursion has signed eigenvalue ρ; the independent proxy has mean shift (x-rh)ρ^t. For finite z, the Bernoulli variances are uniformly rh(1-h)(1+o(1)). In the local limit argument the characteristic-function modulus is bounded by exp(-2σ² sin²(θ/2)) and the centered expansion at θ=w/σ is exp(-w²/2+O(|w|³/√r)); inversion gives uniform local Gaussian error o(r^-1/2), then truncation to O(√r) cells gives an ℓ¹ approximation. The equal-variance Gaussian comparison and whole-number discretization give the stated limit uniformly in x. For z=0 one can apply this at min(t,ceil(2a_N)) and contract, avoiding any use of (1) at arbitrarily late times. For infinite z and u≠h₀, the proxy means are separated by much more than √r, so midpoint Chebyshev and (1) apply; endpoint starts suffice for the worst-start lower bound. The lattice window is bounded, without replacing actual integer-time z by a continuous profile. The packaged exact-rational checker was inspected, not rerun; the proof does not depend on it.
